report.verdict: A senior engineer with strong checkout reliability work and a relevant Go payments project.
write_up: Your resume is strong: at Tidewater, you show platform and checkout work with the scale and results attached! Cascade adds finance reconciliation, and payq brings in idempotent payment retries. That's a compelling combination for this money movement role, though it doesn't yet show ownership of a payouts path.

The GitHub Actions line is a great model: it names what you built and the change in build time. Your experience is easy to follow, but some of the best payments work sits below office activities in the Tidewater role.

Move the payment failover and checkout service work closer to the top, then bring the finance reconciliation and payq work forward. Add context for PostgreSQL and Kafka where you can substantiate it. Your resume is strong enough to get read; the role's requirements and competition will also matter.

cards.cannot_tell: Keep this as a model. It connects a named tool and deliverable to a before-and-after measure without making a recruiter guess what changed.

fit.note: Your Go checkout service and payq project are relevant to the role's payments work, while the finance job gives you a useful reconciliation example. Bring those forward and add any relevant details you can substantiate about your production responsibilities.
